intro: Function code ko naam, inputs aur ek clear output deta hai. Is section me parameters ke saare forms (*args, **kwargs, defaults, keyword-only), closures, lambdas, recursion aur decorators ko practical examples se samjhaya gaya hai.
theory: Function definition par default values evaluate hoti hain; mutable default (list/dict) ek hi object har call me share karta hai — sentinel None use karo.
Positional arguments order se bind hote hain, keyword arguments naam se. `*args` extra positional values ka tuple deta hai, `**kwargs` extra keyword values ka dict.
Python pass-by-object-reference hai: immutable argument rebind karne se caller nahi badalta, mutable argument mutate karne se caller badal jata hai.
Closure tab banta hai jab inner function outer function ke variable ko yaad rakhta hai. `nonlocal` se inner function outer variable ko rebind kar sakta hai.
Decorator ek function hai jo doosra function leta hai aur naya callable return karta hai — logging, timing aur caching ke liye standard pattern.
syntax:
def outer():
    count = 0
    def inner():
        nonlocal count
        count += 1
        return count
    return inner

examples.code:
rows = [('Asha', 91), ('Ravi', 78)]
print(sorted(rows, key=lambda row: row[1], reverse=True))
explain: Lambda chhote key function ke liye useful hai, yahan score par sorting.
Output ko print se verify karo.
Ye Functions & Reusable Python ka basic building block hai.

examples.code:
def counter():
    value = 0
    def bump():
        nonlocal value
        value += 1
        return value
    return bump

c = counter()
print(c(), c())
explain: Closure outer variable ko yaad rakhta hai aur nonlocal se usse badalta hai.
Ek step aur jodne se behaviour kaise badalta hai, dekho.
Input badal kar edge case test karo.
Decorator original function ko wrap karta hai, timing add karta hai aur return value intact rakhta hai.
Ye snippet end-to-end flow dikhata hai.
Output ko project/interview me evidence ki tarah use karo.

realWorld: API handlers aur ETL steps functions me tute hote hain taaki ek step ko independently test kiya ja sake.
Decorators se retry, timing aur auth checks har endpoint par repeat kiye bina lagaye jate hain.
Config functions `**kwargs` se aage ke libraries tak options pass karte hain, isliye signature har option ke liye badalni nahi padti.

interview.q: Mutable default argument khatarnak kyun hai?
interview.a: Default ek hi baar function define hone par banta hai, isliye list/dict har call me share hota hai. Fix: default None rakho aur andar fresh object banao.

interview.q: *args aur **kwargs me fark batao.
interview.a: *args extra positional values ka tuple deta hai; **kwargs extra keyword values ka dict. Dono ko combine karke wrapper functions arguments ko aage pass kar sakte hain.

interview.q: Closure aur global variable me kya antar hai?
interview.a: Closure outer function ke local variable ko capture karta hai, isliye state encapsulated rehti hai. Global variable poore module me visible hota hai aur side effects aasan ho jate hain.

interview.q: Decorator kaise kaam karta hai?
interview.a: Decorator ek callable leta hai aur naya callable return karta hai, jo original ko wrap karta hai. functools.wraps metadata bachata hai; decorator arguments chahte ho to ek extra layer likhni padti hai.

debugging.why: String immutable hai; append list ka method hai. Ye Functions & Reusable Python ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: String concatenation ya join use karo.
debugging.lesson: AttributeError galat type par method call ka signal hai.

debugging.why: Naam ki spelling galat hai; Python namespace me wo naam nahi milta. Ye Functions & Reusable Python ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.lesson: NameError typo ya missing assignment batata hai.

debugging.error: Logic error — sort() None return karta hai, list print nahi hoti
debugging.why: sort() in-place hai aur None deta hai, isliye print None dikhata hai. Ye Functions & Reusable Python ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: sorted() use karo ya pehle sort phir list print karo.
debugging.lesson: Mutating methods ka return value None hota hai — usse assign/print mat karo.

debugging.broken:
prices = [100, 200]
total = 0
for p in prices:
    total = p
print(total)
debugging.error: Logic error — total 200 aata hai, sum 300 hona chahiye
debugging.why: Assignment purani value replace karta hai; accumulator chahiye. Ye Functions & Reusable Python ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: total += p use karo ya sum(prices).
debugging.correct:
prices = [100, 200]
total = 0
for p in prices:
    total += p
print(total)
debugging.lesson: Logic bugs exception nahi dete — chhote sample par expected value likho.

revision: Functions & Reusable Python: revise def_return — Function inputs leta hai aur return se value deta hai.
Functions & Reusable Python: revise default_arg — Default argument call ko chhota banata hai; caller override bhi kar sakta hai.
Functions & Reusable Python: revise keyword_arg — Keyword arguments order se independent hote hain aur call readable banate hain.
Functions & Reusable Python: revise args — *args extra positional values ko tuple me collect karta hai.
Functions & Reusable Python: revise kwargs — **kwargs extra keyword arguments ko dict me collect karta hai.
